comparison: Perfect agreement on visual field partitioning and integration hierarchy (C2-C4, C115-C118, C129). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers affirm this as a major, well-supported finding. OpenEval emphasizes environmental imaging data support; peer reviewers explicitly confirm 'solid evidence for an integration hierarchy' with no challenges.

Partial disagreement on ventrolateral optic flow responses (C18-C22, C25-C26, C81). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about indirect flight height measurement. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 explicitly stating 'measurements of flight height are less solid' and recommending more careful interpretation. Both accept lateral responses but differ on confidence in height measurements.

Strong agreement on dorsal response characterization (C27-C44, C68, C70-C71). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes extensive experimental controls and distinct response characteristics. Peer reviewers accept findings without challenge, acknowledging the separate dorsal pathway and its distinction from optic flow responses.

Agreement on parallel processing and conflict experiments (C45-C51, C82-C84). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights simultaneous execution of responses and independence from stimulus magnitude. Peer reviewers confirm 'solid evidence for integration hierarchy,' though Reviewer 3 notes limitations in temporal statistics and quantification that could be improved.

Agreement on dorsal-lateral conflict hierarchy (C52-C59, C86-C88). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes preferential dorsal avoidance with maintained lateral response. Peer reviewers confirm the hierarchy identification, with Reviewer 3 accepting conclusions after revisions despite noting quantification could be enhanced.

Agreement on dissociation between speed/straightness and distance regulation (C61-C67, C89-C90). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the dissociation occurs despite ventral stimuli generating stronger optic flow. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall hierarchy demonstration, grouped with broader conflict experiment findings.

Agreement on dorsal response characteristics (C68-C74). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing distinction from optic flow paradigm and correlation between speed and lateral movement. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these characterizations as part of the broader dorsal pathway findings (R3), without specific challenge to the mechanistic inferences.

Disagreement on confidence level for canopy avoidance hypothesis (C75-C80, C98-C101). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the interpretation is speculative and requires additional field/comparative studies. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with editor and Reviewer 2 explicitly endorsing the 'avoid crashing into foliage' interpretation, though acknowledging its speculative nature.

Disagreement on confidence level for divergence cue mechanism (C93-C97). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanistic interpretation requires additional targeted experiments. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 3 stating authors 'have made a case for the conclusions as stated,' though the speculative nature is implicit in the claims.

Agreement on parallel operation and conditional weighting synthesis (C82, C85, C91-C92). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes synthesis across multiple conflict experiments and reasonable extrapolation to environmental variation. Peer reviewers accept these conclusions as part of the integration hierarchy evidence, with overlap on C82.

Disagreement on confidence level for comparative interpretations (C102-C114). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting functional interpretations are speculative and require direct testing. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, finding the comparative discussion valuable and not challenging the reasoning, though acknowledging the speculative nature implicitly.

Agreement on key conceptual finding about hierarchy-prevalence mismatch (C119-C128). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this as an important conceptual advance with reasonable inference from data. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse the 'prioritization for generating behavior that supports hawkmoth safety rather than prevalence' conclusion, with Reviewer 1 calling it 'exciting.'

OpenEval identifies background/literature claims (C1, C5-C17, C23-C24, C60, C69) as SUPPORTED by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on novel findings rather than cataloging background information accuracy.
